    fig-pos: 'H'

        \usepackage{caption}

        \usepackage{chngcntr}

        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.35}
        \floatplacement{table}{H}
        \floatplacement{figure}{H}
        \newcounter{parentfig}
        \renewcommand{\thefigure}{C1.\arabic{figure}}
        \renewcommand{\thetable}{C1.\arabic{table}}

  html:
    output-file: "Project 4.21-Ningaloo-3-Appendix C1-q-Data analysis.html"
    fig-dpi: 96
    embed-resources: true
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
          caption,
          .gt_caption,
          .table-caption,
          figcaption,
          .figure-caption,
          .quarto-float-caption,
          .quarto-float-caption-top,
          .quarto-float-tbl figcaption {
            text-align: justify !important;
            text-justify: inter-word;
            hyphens: auto;
          }
        </style>
    include-after-body:
      text: |
        <script>
        // appendix-c-numbering.lua only numbers figures - tables are prefixed
        // here, flat as C1.<n> to match the PDF's \thetable.
        (function () {
          var tbl = 0;
          document.querySelectorAll("#quarto-document-content figcaption.quarto-float-tbl").forEach(function (el) {
            tbl += 1;
            // el.innerHTML re-serialises a non-breaking space as the literal
            // "&nbsp;" entity text, not a whitespace character, so \s alone
            // does not match it - match either form here.
            el.innerHTML = el.innerHTML.replace(
              /^(\s*Table(?:\s|&nbsp;)+)\d+/,
              "$1C1." + tbl
            );
          });
        })();
        </script>
toc: true
execute:

  warning: false

```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Quarto sets the working directory to this folder, so both sources resolve
# locally while here() still points at the project root for the data paths.
source("02_load-model-selection.R")

# gt builders for Table C1.1 and C1.2 live in Gt_model_tables.R so the qmd and
# any standalone use share a single definition (build_report_table,
# build_habitat_model_table, build_fish_model_table).
source("Gt_model_tables.R")

# Significance table at the end of the appendix - see Gt_stats_tables.R.
# Sourced after Gt_model_tables.R, which it reuses helpers from.
source("Gt_stats_tables.R")

habitat_table <- get_habitat_report_table()
fish_table    <- get_fish_report_table()

figdir_src <- file.path(appc_out, "figures")

# HTML cannot load an image by absolute filesystem path the way LaTeX can, so
# each figure is copied into a `figures/` folder beside this document and
# referenced relatively. That path works for both output formats.
figdir_local <- "figures"
dir.create(figdir_local, showWarnings = FALSE)

fig <- function(f) {
  src <- file.path(figdir_src, paste0(name, "_", f))
  if (!file.exists(src)) stop("Figure not found: ", src, "\nRun 03_create-figures.R first.")
  dest <- file.path(figdir_local, paste0(name, "_", f))
  file.copy(src, dest, overwrite = TRUE)
  dest
}

curve_years  <- as.character(sort(unlist(config$years)))
curve_status <- "Fished" # matches factor_ref in 03_create-figures.R

list_and <- function(x) {
  if (!length(x)) return("")
  if (length(x) == 1) return(x)
  paste0(paste(utils::head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(x, 1))
}

# Model selection will not necessarily keep `status` for every fish metric.
# The response curves are therefore only conditioned on status where the
# model contains it, so the caption is assembled from the fitted objects
# rather than hard-coded.
fish_models <- load_final_models()$fish

# Drop the trailing footnote marker - it only belongs on the first mention.
plain_label <- function(keys) sub("\\*$", "", unname(response_labels[keys]))

no_status <- {
  keys <- names(fish_models)[
    !vapply(fish_models, function(m) "status" %in% gam_predictor_set(m), logical(1))
  ]
  plain_label(keys)
}

curve_hold_note <- if (length(no_status)) {
  paste0(" Zone status is held only where model selection retained it: ",
         list_and(no_status), ".")
} else ""

# Significance table (end of appendix) - see Gt_stats_tables.R.
pvalue_table <- build_fish_term_pvalue_table(fish_models, fish_response_order)
```

# Data Analysis

Statistical methods and model selection results underpinning the natural values
reported in Appendix A1.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Benthic ecosystem extent

Both benthic habitat and demersal fish metrics are modelled with survey years
pooled - the model selection results and response curves below therefore each
cover a single, combined dataset rather than one figure per year.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-c1-1
#| tbl-cap: 'Habitat model selection results. Top generalised additive models (GAMs) for predicting the probability of occurrence of key habitats from full subset analyses. Differences between the lowest reported corrected Akaike Information Criterion ($\Delta$AICc), AICc weight ($\omega$AICc), variance explained (R$^2$) and effective degrees of freedom (EDF) are reported for model comparison. Model selection was based on the most parsimonious model (fewest variables - shown in bold) within two units of the lowest AICc. Survey years are pooled for this park, so covariate relationships are fitted once across all of them.'
build_habitat_model_table(habitat_table)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: "85%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: 'Variable importance scores for predicting the probability of occurrence of main habitat categories. Response variables included in the most parsimonious top model are indicated (X), with the colour gradient representing positive (red), zero (white) and negative (blue) relationships. Aspect is a circular variable, so the direction of its relationship should be read from the response curves rather than the colour gradient.'
knitr::include_graphics(fig("habitat-importance.png"))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

```{r}
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: 'Plots of the most parsimonious model found to predict the probability of occurrence of key habitat types. Individual panes display the predicted relationships between model covariates and the probability of occurrence of each habitat class. Solid lines represent predicted Generalized Additive Model (GAM) fits with other variables held constant at their mean value. Dashed lines represent upper and lower standard error bounds around the prediction, and points represent the observed data pooled across all survey years.'
knitr::include_graphics(fig("habitat-response-curves.png"))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Demersal fish assemblage

```{r}
#| label: tbl-c2-1
#| tbl-cap: 'Demersal fish model selection results. Top generalised additive models (GAMs) for predicting the species and abundance distribution of metrics of interest from full subset analyses. Differences between the lowest reported corrected Akaike Information Criterion ($\Delta$AICc), AICc weight ($\omega$AICc), variance explained (R$^2$) and effective degrees of freedom (EDF) are reported for model comparison. Model selection was based on the best model (fewest variables - shown in bold) within two units of the lowest AICc. Zone status (No-Take/Fished) was forced into every candidate model rather than offered as a candidate itself. \*Large Reef Fish Index representing the biomass of all fish greater than 20 cm (B20) has been adapted here for stereo-BRUV data by removing sharks and rays.'
build_fish_model_table(fish_table)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: "85%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: 'Variable importance scores for predicting the probability of demersal fish metrics. Response variables included in the most parsimonious top model are indicated (X), with the colour gradient representing positive (red), zero (white) and negative (blue) relationships. Aspect is a circular variable, so the direction of its relationship should be read from the response curves rather than the colour gradient. \*Large Reef Fish Index representing the biomass of all fish greater than 20 cm (B20) has been adapted here for stereo-BRUV data by removing sharks and rays.'
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fish-importance.png"))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

```{r}
#| out-width: "80%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0('Plots of the best model found to predict the probability of occurrence of key fish groups. Individual panes display the predicted relationships between model covariates and each demersal fish metric. Solid lines represent predicted Generalized Additive Model (GAM) fits with other variables held constant at their mean value, with zone status held at ', curve_status, '.', curve_hold_note, ' Dashed lines represent upper and lower standard error bounds around the prediction, and points represent the observed data pooled across all survey years and zones. \\*Large Reef Fish Index representing the biomass of all fish greater than 20 cm (B20) has been adapted here for stereo-BRUV data by removing sharks and rays.')
knitr::include_graphics(fig("fish-response-curves.png"))
```

#| label: tbl-c3-1
